note: _breviter audias nos pro tua clementia_ – I desire thee of thy clemency to hear us in few words (Douay Version); what we ask of thy courtesy is no more than a brief audience (Knox); höre uns kurz an im Einklang mit deiner Güte (Tusculum-Vulgata). _clementia_, used only here in the Vulgate New Testament, is a Roman virtue typically expected from someone in a position of authority, e.g., of an emperor. In this passage, Paul’s appeal is to the _clementia_ of Felix, Roman procurator of Judaea. On _clementia_, see the glossary s.v. (Chapter 19.2).
